text.p: Libertel, operator of the Netherlands' second GSM mobile telephone network, said on Wednesday its subscriptions had surpassed the 150,000 mark within a year of the network's launch.
"In the first year of its existence Libertel realised a growth of 25 percent above its prognosis and expects to exceed the mark of 200,000 connections this year," it said.

Libertel, 52 percent owned by Dutch financial group ING and 35 percent owned by British mobile phone operator Vodafone, said it was gaining 600 subscribers a day and expected this rate to pick up now it offered full national coverage.
Libertel said the Netherlands had 870,000 mobile phone connections at present, adding that it expected this number to rise to four million by the year 2000.
It said that since it began to compete against the mobile telephone networks of Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV, the cost of mobile phone calls in the Netherlands had fallen 40 percent.
